newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast's Essy withdraws from U.N. race.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast's Essy withdraws from U.N. race.

text.p: Ivory Coast's foreign minister, Amara Essy, formally withdrew from the race for the next U.N. secretary-general, Ivorian state television reported on Friday.

His move followed news that Ghana's Kofi Annan, who heads U.N. peacekeeping operations, had won the unanimous support of Security Council members in an unofficial poll after France dropped a veto threat.

Essy, the 1994-95 U.N. General Assembly president, had been Annan's closest rival. He won seven votes on Thursday against Annan's 14 but those opposing him included two permanent veto-wielding members, the United States and Britain.
Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali had hoped for a second five-year term from January 1 but was blocked by a U.S. veto. Washington insists the United Nations needs new leadership to carry out reforms.
